clarity.justification: The minimal-pair manipulation—“swap only the matrix verb” over identical, balanced true/false propositions—directly tests the directional prediction that “‘know’ raises complement-truth activation” while a broken gate produces “near-identical complement encodings across verbs.” This is falsifiable because an absent know–believe shift, or a shift equally present for non-factive verbs, would contradict the proposed mechanism, but “raises,” “near-identical,” and “factivity-gate strength” lack numeric decision thresholds. The plan also leaves the truth probe’s training labels, layer/token aggregation, and protection against probe sensitivity to lexical verb identity unspecified, so an expert would need clarification before interpreting the measured shift as an internal belief update rather than a correlational encoding difference.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is “path patching from the verb token to complement tokens to identify heads carrying the factive signal”; path patching, head ablation, probing, and steering are supported by standard interpretability tooling, but the proposal does not specify patch sources, destinations, layers, or the candidate-selection rule, leaving meaningful custom design work. The named behavioral resources and paradigms—“FactBank, MegaVeridicality” and “held-out KaBLE-style items”—and the required probe/patching methods are plausible existing components, although no exact model checkpoints or existing truth probe are identified. Resources receive partial credit for the concrete “~3k items,” but model sizes, checkpoint count, probe-training sample allocation, and intervention scale remain generic. The refuting branch is runnable because identical complements, balanced true/false items, and non-factive controls “{know, believe, think, be convinced, be aware}” permit a null or non-specific effect, though the acknowledged “verb frequency and collocational confounds” are not accompanied by an explicit matching control.
